newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 21.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Monday:
- New York City's economy has begun to recover from its slump as profits rise on Wall Street.
- Sports Team Analysis and Tracking Systems Inc and Motorola Inc are appealing a court injunction against the dissemination of National Basketball Association scores.

- Computer corporate officials see California's proposition to lower the barrier to class-action lawsuits in cases of stock fraud as a threat to the country's technological heartland in Silicon Valley.
- Lars Nyberg, chairman of NCR Corp, is leading a financial turnaround at the company, which has been losing money ever since it was taken over by AT&T Corp in 1991.
- General Motors Corp and the Canadian Automobile Workers union failed to reach an agreement over the weekend for a new labor contract.
- The U.S. Labor Department said fewer oversease apparel makers were using child labor due to negative publicity.
- Exponential Technology Inc plans to launch a new version of the Power PC mircoprocessor on Monday that might help Apple Computer Inc recover lost ground in the personal computers market.
- Leo Burnett Co plans to return to the "basics ...focusing on developing superior, brand-building advertizing" following its loss of the United Airlines account last week.
- U.S. Robotics Corp plans to launch a new modem have enticed traders on Wall Street.
- U.S. magazines are enjoying a good year as they earn more revenue for every page of advertizing.
- Publishing house P.F. Collier plans to release the first uncensored encyclopedia on Russia since the Russian Revolution.
